accuracy.reason: Roles-and-exchange and shared-protocol objectives are accurate: roles are connection-specific; HTTP fields and application semantics are distinct. Live RFC sections 3.3, 3.4, 1.3 and 9.2.2 support these boundaries.

evidence.quote: These are roles in an interaction, not types of computer.

mechanisms.reason: Session-state objective explains the local-memory dependency and externalization consequence. Explain-one-interaction connects checks, allowed work, stored state and uncertain delivery without implying rollback.

evidence.quote: Moving state to shared storage helps replace handlers but leaves a storage dependency.

coherence.reason: All five card objectives build from roles to rules, session placement, benefits/dependencies and a complete flow; prerequisites are sufficient. Inspected diagram and shared dialog/CSS: zero-based mapping aligns; stateful diagram is a local-session example clarified by prose. No runtime UI test performed.

evidence.quote: Connect the request, responsibilities, data and outcome. Component names alone do not explain behavior.

decisions.reason: Benefits-and-dependencies objective connects central reuse to latency, rejection and outage, then supports client/server placement decisions and uncertain-retry reasoning.

evidence.quote: Overload can increase waiting or require rejection; the client/server model alone guarantees neither capacity nor availability.

clarity.reason: Plain definitions of roles, protocol, API and session context support the stated basic-programming audience; reminders reinforce consequential distinctions.

evidence.quote: Stateless does not mean no stored data. Stateless servers can use a shared database.

outcomes.reason: All five criteria supported: learner traces request/response, names roles independent of hardware/browser/location, explains both roles in one program, protocol rules, every HTTP field and application success/error meaning.

All six criteria supported: retained session context, local-memory dependence, request/shared-store context, replacement and storage dependency, shared reuse, latency/failure/overload and no inherent scalability/availability guarantee.

All three criteria supported: generic read/change flow checks before work, distinguishes persistent data and session context, and connects explicit error versus absent response to possible completed work. Chosen storage arrangement is explicitly conditional.

sourceChecks.claim: Live RFC 9110 sections 3.3-3.5 explicitly distinguish client/server roles and permit the same program in both; client types extend beyond browsers.
Live RFC 9110 sections 1.3 and 3.4 specify requests, responses, methods, target, headers, content and interpretation. OWASP REST Security followup verifies server-side access checks.

Live Azure autoscaling application-design section requires avoiding instance affinity and recommends stateless services; shared durable state and downstream bottlenecks confirm the stated remaining dependency.

Live MDN sections on differing purposes and server-side uses support shared data/rules, client presentation and authorized access. Azure autoscaling followup verifies finite capacity, waiting and rejection; network failure reasoning also follows RFC transport/retry discussion.
Live RFC 9110 section 9.2.2 explicitly allows that an original request succeeded before communication failed and warns against blind non-idempotent retry.
